1.1 Preparation of buffers and working area for cellular fractionation. Prepare all buffers on the day of fractionation before collecting cells. Prepare CLB, SB, NWB, GB, NLB, and CRS buffers (see Materials section 1.1 for buffer components) and store all solutions on ice.
1.1 Preparation of buffers and working area for cellular fractionation. Prepare all buffers on the day of fractionation before collecting cells. Make sure tabletop centrifuge is at 4 °C.
Denature the RNA sample (from the cellular fractionation, section 3.3.3) and 5 µl of the oGAB11 control (10 µM; Table 1) for 2 min at 80 °C in a Thermomixer. Place on ice.
Denature the RNA sample (from the cellular fractionation, section 1.3.3) and 5 µl of the oGAB11 control (10 µM; Table 1 in the Materials section) for 2 min at 80 °C in a Thermomixer. Place on ice.

substeps.instruction: Count out 1x10^7 cells as input for each fractionation, including a western blot control sample.
Collect cells by centrifugation at 500g for 2 min at room temperature.
Wash with 10 ml of PBS (room temperature).
Collect cells by centrifugation at 500g for 2 min at room temperature.
Optionally add Drosophila S2 spike-in cells to the sample.
Repeat the wash and centrifugation steps.
Completely remove supernatant by aspiration.

steps.title: Cell Lysis and Nuclei Isolation
steps.instruction: Isolate the nuclei fraction from the cells.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µl of CLB to cells using a cut P1000 pipette tip and mix by pipetting up and down ten times.
Transfer sample to an RNase-free 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube and incubate on ice for 5 min.
Prepare 500 µl of SB in an RNase-free 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Layer the cell lysate onto the SB using a cut 1,000 µl pipette tip.
Centrifuge at 16,000g for 10 min at 4 °C to collect nuclei.
Completely pipette off the supernatant (retain as cytoplasmic fraction for western blot).
Wash nuclei pellet with 800 µl of NWB by inverting the tube or pipetting.
Centrifuge at 1,150g for 1 min at 4 °C and completely remove the supernatant.

steps.title: Chromatin Fraction Isolation
steps.instruction: Isolate the chromatin pellet from the nuclei.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µl of GB to the nuclei and resuspend the pellet using a cut 1,000 µl tip by pipetting up and down.
Transfer the nuclei suspension to a new 1.5 ml RNase-free microcentrifuge tube.
Layer 200 µl of NLB onto the nuclei suspension and mix by pulsed vortexing.
Incubate on ice for 2 min.
Centrifuge at 18,500g for 2 min at 4 °C to collect the chromatin pellet.
Completely remove the supernatant (retain as nucleoplasm fraction for western blot).

steps.title: Nascent RNA Preparation
steps.instruction: Extract and purify nascent RNA from the chromatin pellet.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µl CRS to the chromatin pellet, transfer to a new 1.5 ml tube, and resuspend.
Add 700 µl of QIAzol to the resuspended chromatin.
Solubilize the pellet by slowly pipetting up and down using a 1-ml syringe with a 22G needle until homogeneous.
Purify RNA using the miRNeasy mini kit (or micro kit for small cell numbers) according to manufacturer's instructions, including optional DNase treatment.
Measure RNA quantity and quality using a NanoDrop (typical yield 20–30 µg).
Store isolated RNA at -80 °C.

steps.title: Linker Ligation
steps.instruction: Ligate linkers to the nascent RNA.

substeps.instruction: Spray all work surfaces and pipettes with RNase away.
Prepare linker ligation mix for each RNA sample and the oGAB11 control in 0.2-ml RNase-free PCR tubes; mix until homogeneous.
Add 1 µl Truncated T4 RNA ligase 2 (200U) to each sample.
Incubate in a thermal cycler for 10-16 hours at 16 °C.
Place on ice and add 0.7 µl of 0.5 M EDTA to stop the reaction.

steps.title: RNA Fragmentation Calibration
steps.instruction: Determine the optimal fragmentation time using a test sample (Box 2).

substeps.instruction: Take 9 samples of RNA (~1ug each), resuspend in 8uL RNase-free water, and add 12uL of linker ligation mix (excluding linker and ligase).
Add 20 µl of 2× alkaline fragmentation solution to each and mix.
Fragment samples at 95 °C in a thermal cycler for 0, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, and 50 minutes.
Purify fragmented RNA using RNA Clean & Concentrator-5 kit (Zymo) and elute in 10 uL of 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.0).
Prepare RNA ladder: 1.0 µl RNA control ladder + 9 µl RNase-free H2O + 10 µl 2× TBU denaturing sample buffer.
Prepare RNA samples by adding 10 µl 2× TBU denaturing sample buffer to each.
Denature samples and ladder for 2 min at 80 °C, then place on ice.
Prerun a 15% (wt/vol) polyacrylamide TBE-urea gel at 200 V for 15 min in 1× TBE after flushing wells.
Load gel and separate by PAGE at 200 V for 65 min.
Stain in 50 ml gel staining solution for 5 min at room temperature on a shaker in a black box.
Visualize under blue/UV light; optimal time is when most RNA is between 40 and 110 nt.

steps.title: RNA Fragmentation and Size Selection
steps.instruction: Fragment the ligated RNA and select for the required size range.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 µl of 2× alkaline fragmentation solution to each ligation sample (except oGAB11 control) and mix.
Incubate at 95 °C in a thermal cycler for the calibrated time.
Purify fragmented RNA using RNA Clean & Concentrator-5 kit (Zymo) and elute in 10 uL of 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.0).
Prepare RNA ladder and un-ligated oGAB11 control: 1.0 µl ladder/oGAB11 + 9 µl RNase-free H2O + 10 µl 2× TBU denaturing sample buffer.
Prepare all samples (including ligated oGAB11) by adding 10 µl 2× TBU denaturing sample buffer and mixing.
Denature samples and ladder for 2 min at 80 °C, then place on ice.
Prerun a 15% (wt/vol) polyacrylamide TBE-urea gel at 200 V for 15 min in 1× TBE.
Load gel and separate by PAGE at 200 V for 65 min.
Stain in 50 ml gel staining solution for 5 min at room temperature on a shaker in a black box.
Excise the region between 40 and 110 nt for fragmented RNA and a narrow band ~55 nt for ligated oGAB11.
Perform rapid gel extraction (Box 3) and elute RNA using RNA Clean & Concentrator-5 kit (Zymo) with 10 uL of 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.0).

steps.title: Reverse Transcription
steps.instruction: Convert the size-selected RNA into cDNA.

substeps.instruction: Prepare RT reaction mix in a 0.2-ml RNase-free PCR tube and store on ice.
Add 4.6 µl of RT reaction mix to 10 µl of the RNA sample and oGAB11 control.
Denature mixtures for 2 min at 80 °C in a thermal cycler, then place on ice.
Add 1.3 µl of SUPERase.In/DTT mix and mix well.
Add 0.8 µl of SuperScript III (200 U/µl) and mix.
Incubate for 30 min at 48 °C in a thermal cycler.

steps.title: RNA Degradation
steps.instruction: Remove the RNA template after cDNA synthesis.

substeps.instruction: Add 1.8 µl of 1 N NaOH, mix well, and incubate for 20 min at 98 °C.
Neutralize by adding 1.8 µl of 1 N HCl, mix well, and place on ice.

steps.title: cDNA Size Selection
steps.instruction: Select and extract the cDNA of the appropriate length.

substeps.instruction: Prepare DNA control ladder: 1.0 µl ladder + 9 µl RNase-free H2O + 10 µl 2× TBU denaturing sample buffer.
Add 20 µl of 2× TBU denaturing sample buffer to the cDNA sample and oGAB11 cDNA control and mix.
Prerun a 10% (wt/vol) polyacrylamide TBE-urea gel at 200 V for 15 min in 1× TBE.
Load gel (20 uL per lane, split each sample into two lanes) and separate by PAGE at 200 V for 65 min.
Stain in 50 ml gel staining solution for 5 min at room temperature on a shaker in a black box.
Excise region between ~85 and 160 nt for cDNA sample and a narrow band ~85 nt for oGAB11 control.
Perform rapid gel extraction (Box 3), combining the two lanes of one sample into a single tube.
Elute cDNA using the Oligo kit (Zymo) with 15 uL of 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0).

steps.title: cDNA Circularization
steps.instruction: Circularize the cDNA for subsequent PCR amplification.

substeps.instruction: Prepare circularization mix and store on ice.
In a 0.2-ml RNase-free PCR tube, add 4 µl of circularization mix to 15 µl of the cDNA sample and oGAB11 control; mix well.
Add 1 µl of CircLigase (100 U/µl) and mix.
Incubate in a thermal cycler for 60 min at 60 °C, then 10 min at 80 °C.
Optional: perform specific depletion of highly abundant mature RNAs.

steps.title: PCR Amplification Optimization
steps.instruction: Determine the minimum number of PCR cycles required (Box 4).

substeps.instruction: Prepare PCR master mix for four pilot reactions for each cDNA sample and oGAB11 control; store on ice.
Dispense 19 µl of PCR master mix into 0.2-ml RNase-free PCR tubes.
Add 1 µl of circularized cDNA and mix.
Perform pilot amplifications (Table 2: 98°C 30s, then cycles of 98°C 10s, 60°C 10s, 72°C 5s). Remove one tube after 6, 8, 10, and 12 cycles.
Add 3.4 µl of 6× DNA loading dye to each tube.
Prepare DNA control ladder: 1.0 µl ladder + 9 µl DNase-free H2O + 2 µl 6× DNA loading dye.
Separate products on an 8% (wt/vol) TBE gel at 180 V for 55 min.
Stain in 50 ml gel staining solution for 5 min at room temperature on a shaker in a black box.
Visualize under blue/UV light; optimal cycles show a clear band at ~150 nt with no higher-molecular-weight products (typically 6-8 cycles).

steps.title: Library PCR Amplification
steps.instruction: Amplify the NET-seq library using optimized cycles.

substeps.instruction: Prepare PCR mix for the cDNA sample and oGAB11 control; store on ice.
Put 19 µl of PCR master mix in a 0.2-ml RNase-free PCR tube.
Add 1 µl of circularized cDNA and mix.
Perform PCR amplifications using the determined optimal number of cycles.
Prepare DNA control ladder: 1.0 µl ladder + 9 µl DNase-free H2O + 2 µl 6× DNA loading dye.
Add 3.4 µl of 6× DNA loading dye to each PCR sample tube.
Separate on an 8% (wt/vol) TBE gel at 180 V for 55 min.
Stain in 50 ml gel staining solution for 5 min at room temperature on a shaker in a black box.
Excise the broad band at ~150 nt (avoid the ~120 nt band).
Perform the first four steps of rapid gel extraction (Box 3).
Add 670 µl of DNA soaking buffer and mix.
Incubate overnight at room temperature in a Thermomixer at 1,500 r.p.m.
Transfer gel slurry into a microcentrifuge tube filter using a cut 1,000 µl tip.
Centrifuge at 20,000g for 3 min at room temperature and transfer eluate to a new 1.5 ml tube.
Precipitate by adding 2 µl of 15 mg/ml GlycoBlue and 680 µl of isopropanol; mix and incubate at -20 °C for ≥1 h.
Centrifuge at 20,000g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Wash pellet with 750 µl of 80% (vol/vol) ice-cold ethanol.
Centrifuge at 20,000g for 2 min at 4 °C, remove supernatant, and air-dry pellet for 10 min at room temperature.
Resuspend the library in 7-10 µl of 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0).

steps.title: Library Quantification and Sequencing
steps.instruction: Quantify the library and perform Illumina sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 1:5 dilution: 1 µl library + 4 µl 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0).
Quantify 1 µl of diluted library using Qubit fluorometer with dsDNA HS assay kit.
Characterize 1 µl of diluted library on Agilent Bioanalyzer using high-sensitivity DNA analysis kit.
Sequence the human library from the 3' end (75 bp single-end) on Illumina platform using oLSC006 as a custom primer (target 100-200 million reads).

steps.title: Bioinformatics Analysis
steps.instruction: Process sequencing data to determine RNA polymerase coverage.

substeps.instruction: Displace 5' end random barcode (UMI) to the read identifier line and save as a separate fastq file.
Align fastq files (with and without UMI) to human reference genome using STAR (concatenate with Drosophila fasta if spike-in was used).
Filter out RT mispriming alignments (reads lacking UMI that align well both with and without UMI displacement).
Filter out alignments mapping to multiple locations using MAPQ values.
Remove PCR duplicates (alignments sharing position, strand, chromosome, UMI, and CIGAR score).
Remove alignments from splicing intermediates (3' ends of annotated exons and introns).
Use HTseq to generate a bedgraph coverage file from the 5' end of reads (without UMI) on the opposite strand.
Adjust nucleoplasmic and chromatin fraction volumes to match the cytoplasmic fraction volume using 1× PBS.
Add 50 µl of 2× SDS buffer to 50 µl of each fraction and boil at 95 °C for 5 min.
Separate samples by standard SDS-PAGE (load 10 µl per lane).
Probe membrane overnight at 4 °C with Pol II CTD Ser2-P (3E10, 1:1,000) and Pol II CTD Ser5-P (3E8, 1:1,000) antibodies.

steps.title: Rapid Gel Extraction (Box 3)
steps.instruction: General procedure for extracting nucleic acids from polyacrylamide gels.

substeps.instruction: Pierce the bottom of a 0.5-ml RNase-free tube with a 21G needle and place it inside a 1.5-ml RNase-free tube.
Place the gel slice into the pierced 0.5-ml tube.
Centrifuge at 20,000g for 4 min at room temperature.
Add 200 µl of RNase-free H2O to the chopped-up gel and mix.
Incubate for 10 min at 70 °C in a Thermomixer.
Vortex for 30 s at medium intensity.
Transfer the mixture into a microcentrifuge tube filter using a cut 1,000-µl tip.
Centrifuge at 20,000g for 3 min at room temperature.
